answer: Anchor each identity to real silicon. Minting requires a remote attestation quote from a hardware vault — a secure enclave or TPM bound to one physical chip, answering a fresh per-epoch nonce. A sybil farm finds no haven here: one server cannot forge a thousand distinct chips, so an operator would need a ferrous warehouse of real devices, each quoted separately. Duplicate attestation fingerprints across identities flag clones instantly, and hardware capital costs scale linearly while the fake identities do not.
